issue_9_replacements.quote: The numeric effect of Gear Ratio and Max Power was not decoded.
issue_9_replacements.replacement: Gear Ratio selects r=1,2,4,8,16,32. Powered joint speed scales as 1/r. Max Power P is the stored fraction of the editor percentage and scales motor capacity linearly: hinge maximum impulse is F*r^2*P, slider maximum force is F*r*P. Velocity motors additionally multiply capacity by electrical/damage availability A. Suspension uses its separate force law.

issue_9_replacements.quote: How the gear ratio trades speed for holding torque and what Max Power scales were not recovered numerically; measure with a torque meter on a torque-capable joint.
issue_9_replacements.replacement: Doubling ratio halves commanded speed, quadruples the hinge impulse cap and doubles slider force capacity. Max Power scales capacity, not the target speed. Hinge holding torque in internal units is Jmax/dt for the physics solver timestep dt; do not equate Jmax to SI torque or assume one solve per component update.

open_questions.ruled_out: Definition max_motor_force cannot be quoted as torque: hinge uses raw impulse, slider divides force by solver fps. No torque-meter conversion was traced.
Selected suspension setup constructs btSliderConstraint, not btGeneric6DofSpring. Selected update has no independent spring or damper coefficient; it uses a force-limited velocity motor.

open_questions.item: Transfer network loss or mechanical RPS/torque through pass-through joints
open_questions.ruled_out: The powered hinge/slider motor equations do not establish transfer-network loss. Gear Ratio here is motor gearing, not a proven gearbox formula for pass-through shafts.

open_questions.item: Absolute editor placement to world-coordinate signs
open_questions.ruled_out: Local sign reversal and axis handling are recovered; placement transforms were not reduced to a world-space orientation table.
